purpose: Assess ASVS V5 File Handling against the platform's real upload and download surfaces, producing per-requirement PASS and FAIL backed by file-bound evidence rather than by chapter-level assumption.
requiredInvariants: Each of the 13 V5 requirements carries its own decision and its own evidence; none inherits a verdict from its chapter or its neighbour.
PASS is expressible only where the control is named by file and re-verified on every run.
FAIL is held to the same standard as PASS: it must name where the gap is and carry a condition that stops holding once the gap is closed.
A FAIL is recorded and reported, never resolved by editing product logic - that is outside the scope of this programme.
A requirement that cannot be assessed honestly stays PENDING_APPLICABILITY_REVIEW and NOT_ASSESSED.
Requirement prose from the standard must not be copied into the evidence artifact.
Proprietary source must not be sent to any external service; only the pinned public standard is downloaded.
No product logic, dependency, production, REG.RU, DNS or database change.
acceptance: PRESENT_AT_PATH holds only when every named path carries the control; a partial result does not satisfy it.
A decision naming a path that is no longer tracked stops holding.
ABSENT_AT_PATH stops holding once the gap it describes is closed, and the requirement returns to assessment.
A path-bound condition declaring no paths does not hold.
A FAIL without evidence or without a condition is rejected.
All 13 V5 requirements are decided: 4 PASS, 9 FAIL.
finalPass stays false and the blockers name the remaining pending and failing requirements.
The concurrent-scope guard accepts exactly the six authorized paths.
